statements.impact_statement: The glob CLI -c/--cmd command injection requires invoking the glob command line with attacker-controlled file names. The glob CLI is not on the image filesystem (the npm tree that vendors it is removed at build time), no JavaScript package manager ships (SEC-IMG-03), and the runtime starts only node /app/bymorning.mjs. The only child processes the bundle can start are fixed cloud-SDK credential helpers (Azure CLI and PowerShell fallbacks, AWS credential_process), none of which is glob. Matched only through the Node 22 RPM metadata.

pacote is npm's package fetcher. npm and its entire dependency tree (including pacote) are removed from the runtime image; the match is a residual RPM-metadata association with the RHEL nodejs module. No package resolution, git fetch, or npm operation occurs at runtime.

The flaw is in the WebSocket client of the undici copy vendored inside Node 22 (globalThis.WebSocket): a malicious server crashes the process during the opening handshake. No shipped composition constructs that client. The Gateway's only WebSocket client is the Kubernetes Code Interpreter's pods/exec channel to the operator-configured Kubernetes API server, which uses the separate ws library (8.21.3), not undici. The model SDK's optional WebSocket transport needs a WebSocket constructor layer that no shipped composition provides (source-audited).

The flaw is in undici's BalancedPool constructor discarding custom TLS certificate validation. The runtime never constructs a BalancedPool: the application's HTTP client is Effect's FetchHttpClient over Node's global fetch, which uses the default Agent, and the shipped bundle carries no undici copy of its own (checked in the image).

The cross-origin cache poisoning requires explicitly composing undici's cache or deduplicate interceptors onto a Client/Pool. No shipped code composes those interceptors (source-audited); the default dispatcher behind Node's global fetch does not include them.

The pcre2_dfa_match out-of-bounds write is reachable only through PCRE2 consumers. Node.js executes regular expressions on V8's own engine; node and libnode do not link PCRE2 (verified with ldd in the image). The image's only PCRE2 consumer is libselinux, used by OS utilities the runtime never executes: the container runs a single non-root Node process.

The pcre2_jit_match memory corruption is reachable only through PCRE2 consumers. Node.js uses V8's RegExp engine and does not link PCRE2; the only PCRE2 consumer in the image (libselinux, for OS utilities) is never executed at runtime.

The out-of-bounds write requires an application that compiles an attacker-controlled regular expression with PCRE2's JIT interfaces. Node.js compiles regular expressions with V8, not PCRE2; node and libnode do not link PCRE2 (verified with ldd in the image), and the only PCRE2 consumer in the image (libselinux, for OS utilities) is never executed by the single non-root Node process. Red Hat has not published a fixed RHEL 9 build.

The mount(8) TOCTOU requires a local unprivileged user with write access to an ancestor of a user/users fstab mount target. The container runs one non-root process (uid 65532), has no fstab user mounts, no mount execution, and no interactive or multi-user access path.

The flaw is missing connection-level flow control in OpenSSL's QUIC implementation. The runtime serves TLS over TCP only and uses no QUIC listener or client, so the vulnerable path is never exercised. Matched against the RHEL 9 OpenSSL RPM; no fix is published yet.

The flaw is in OpenSSL's DTLS handshake retransmission. The runtime uses TLS over TCP only and never initiates or accepts DTLS, so the vulnerable path is never exercised. Matched against the RHEL 9 OpenSSL RPM; no fix is published yet.

The flaw is in the http-cache-semantics package, which the Node 22 RPM carries only inside npm's vendored tree. npm and /usr/lib/node_modules are removed from the image at build time (no http-cache-semantics file is on the image filesystem), and the application does not use http-cache-semantics (source-audited). Residual RPM-metadata match.

path-to-regexp 6.1.0 is pinned by @vercel/routing-utils, used by the documentation site's Vercel adapter only. The shipped server router does not use path-to-regexp; it is absent from the bundle and image.

http-cache-semantics 4.2.0 enters the lockfile only through astro, the documentation-site generator (packages/docs). It is not imported by the server bundle and is absent from the image. No patched version is published.

statements.impact_statement: brace-expansion stack exhaustion in parseCommaParts on crafted brace patterns (GHSA-6j4f-fj2g-mc7p). npm's copy is removed with /usr/lib/node_modules (empty in the image; no brace-expansion file on the filesystem). The Node 22 RPM's only remaining copy is inlined in Node's internal minimatch, which is reachable only through path.matchesGlob and fs.glob/globSync/promises.glob; neither the bundle nor any bundled plugin calls them (checked in the image). The application's own brace-expansion copies (5.0.12, 2.1.7, 1.1.21) are fixed versions. Red Hat lists no fixed build.

brace-expansion uncontrolled recursion in expand_ on deeply nested brace groups (GHSA-qhr7-859c-m2p7). The Node 22 RPM's only remaining copy is inlined in Node's internal minimatch (present: a deeply nested pattern exhausts the stack through path.matchesGlob in the image) and is reachable only through path.matchesGlob and fs.glob/globSync/promises.glob, which neither the bundle nor any bundled plugin calls. npm's copy is removed. The application's own brace-expansion copies (5.0.12, 2.1.7, 1.1.21) are fixed versions. Red Hat lists no fixed build.

undici's Agent drops a function-valued tls option (such as a custom checkServerIdentity for pinning) during option cloning (GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx). Node 22.23.2 vendors undici 6.28.0 but does not expose its Agent; the shipped bundle contains no undici code, dispatcher override, or setGlobalDispatcher call (checked in the image), so global fetch runs on the default Agent with no tls options and there is no custom verification callback to drop.

Cache-key confusion when undici's redirect and cache interceptors are composed with a shared store (GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26) affects undici 7.0.0-7.30.0 and 8.0.0-8.12.1. Node 22.23.2 vendors undici 6.28.0 (process.versions in the image), outside the affected range; no shipped code composes interceptors either.

The WebSocket-over-HTTP/2 failed-handshake crash (GHSA-qq8j-7v2v-3rwp) affects only undici 8.11.0 and 8.11.1. Node 22.23.2 vendors undici 6.28.0 (process.versions in the image), which does not contain the vulnerable code.

statements.action_statement: Node 22.23.2's vendored undici 6.28.0 (affected range 6.23.0-6.29.0; GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c): a server that returns more than five content codings and closes the connection crashes the process even though the fetch() rejection is caught (reproduced in the image: unhandled UND_ERR_SOCKET, exit code 1). Impact is denial of service only: the Gateway process exits, dropping in-flight requests and background work on that replica, and is restarted by the container orchestrator; no data exposure. Exposure is limited to global-fetch destinations chosen by the operator or a Workspace administrator, or advertised by them: model provider endpoints, the OIDC issuer, admin-registered remote MCP servers and their OAuth authorization servers, and first-party plugin vendor APIs. Model-steered URLs use the node:http web-fetch Tool, not undici. No workaround exists upstream. Red Hat lists no fixed Node 22 RPM yet; the upstream fix is undici 6.29.1. Remediated by the first base-image update whose Node 22 RPM carries it (POA&M, section 13 SLA).

Node 22.23.2's vendored undici 6.28.0 (affected range 4.2.1-6.29.0; GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm): an HTTPS server that negotiates TLS 1.2 and renegotiates with a different CA-trusted certificate whose hostname does not match triggers an uncaught assertion that terminates the process. Outbound TLS is not restricted to 1.3 (Node's default minimum is TLS 1.2), so any global-fetch endpoint can trigger it; not reproduced. Impact is denial of service only: the Gateway process exits, dropping in-flight requests and background work on that replica, and is restarted by the container orchestrator. Exposure is limited to global-fetch destinations chosen by the operator or a Workspace administrator, or advertised by them: model provider endpoints, the OIDC issuer, admin-registered remote MCP servers and their OAuth authorization servers, and first-party plugin vendor APIs. Model-steered URLs use the node:http web-fetch Tool, not undici. The upstream workaround (TLS 1.3-only outbound) is not applied because it would also constrain database and cloud-SDK TLS and is untested. Red Hat lists no fixed Node 22 RPM yet; the upstream fix is undici 6.29.1. Remediated by the first base-image update whose Node 22 RPM carries it (POA&M, section 13 SLA).

statements.impact_statement: GnuTLS Common Name fallback hostname-verification bypass. Node.js uses OpenSSL for TLS: node and libnode do not link GnuTLS (verified with ldd and the running process's /proc/self/maps in the image). The image's only GnuTLS consumer is /usr/bin/dirmngr (GnuPG), which the single non-root Node process never executes. Red Hat has not published a fixed RHEL 9 build.

The libblkid DOS extended-partition integer overflow requires a libblkid consumer to probe a crafted disk image or removable medium. node and libnode do not link libblkid or libmount (verified with ldd in the image). The image's libblkid consumers (GLib/gio tools, microdnf/libdnf, librhsm) are never executed by the single non-root Node process (uid 65532), which probes no block devices. Red Hat has not published a fixed RHEL 9 build.

statements.impact_statement: launch-editor (bundled by vite 7.3.6 and 8.2.0) is reached only through the Vite development server's open-in-editor middleware, and the flaw (an fs.existsSync() check that can be bypassed on Windows) applies to Windows only. Vite is workspace build tooling: the Gateway image ships the built UI assets and no development server. A search of all 8 layers of the 1.3.0 Gateway image finds no launch-editor or vite file, and the bundle contains neither name. Fixed upstream in vite 7.3.7 and 8.2.4; the lockfile versions are not moved in this release.

The Node.js DNS resolver APIs (dns.resolve*, backed by c-ares) truncate a hostname containing an embedded NUL. Neither first-party code nor any bundled dependency calls them: the shipped bundle imports node:dns once, for dns.lookup (getaddrinfo, not c-ares) in the web-fetch egress screen, and no resolve4/resolve6/resolveAny/resolveCname/resolveMx/resolveNs/resolveSrv/resolveTxt/resolvePtr/resolveSoa/resolveNaptr/resolveCaa reference exists in any of the image's 64 application chunks. No vendor fix exists yet for Node 22.23.2; revisit with the first base-image update that carries one.

statements.action_statement: Node 22.23.2's TLS stack: checkServerIdentity can accept a certificate that does not identify the peer when a non-canonical numeric hostname (for example 0x7f.1 or 2130706433) is connected to, allowing server impersonation by an attacker who is already positioned on the network path. Exposure is narrow: outbound destinations (model providers, the OIDC issuer, admin-registered remote MCP servers, web fetch) are parsed as URLs, and the WHATWG URL parser rewrites every numeric form to a canonical dotted quad before the hostname reaches TLS (verified for 0x7f.1, 2130706433, 0177.0.0.1 and 127.1); the only first-party tls.connect calls that take a raw hostname string are test fixtures, and the database host comes from the operator's DATABASE_URL. Not audited: every third-party client's handling of a hostname string it is given directly. No vendor fix exists yet; remediated by the first base-image update whose Node RPM carries one. Tracked on the POA&M in the vulnerability triage.

statements.impact_statement: @azure/msal-node 6.0.1 (via @azure/identity 4.13.3) can disclose authorization-code-flow parameters to an attacker-controlled endpoint. The code path is MsalClient.getTokenByAuthorizationCode, whose only caller in @azure/identity is AuthorizationCodeCredential. The Gateway constructs only DefaultAzureCredential (backends/azure and app/host/src/azure.ts), whose chain is VS Code, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell, azd, broker, environment, workload identity and managed identity: none uses the authorization-code flow. The fix is 7.1.0, a major version that @azure/identity 4.13.3 (^6) does not accept; move with the next @azure/identity release.
